notes.meaning: As human populations grew, men from the godly family line of Seth married women from the ungodly line of Cain. Instead of choosing partners based on faith and godliness, they looked only at physical beauty and their own desires. These mixed marriages caused true religion to fade and opened the door to widespread corruption across the world.

differ.view: Some hold that the sons of God were fallen angels who took human bodies and married human women to corrupt the human race.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic commentators reject the Sethite view because daughters of men naturally means humanity in general, and note that these unions occurred both before and after the flood.

notes.meaning: God warned that his Holy Spirit would not continue pleading with human hearts forever through preachers and inward convictions. People had become completely ruled by their sinful fleshly desires and refused to change. In his mercy, God granted a countdown of 120 years as a time of grace for them to repent before the flood arrived.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars interpret the 120 years as a new maximum lifespan set for human beings rather than a waiting period before the flood.

notes.meaning: The Nephilim were violent tyrants who used their power to attack others and take whatever they wanted. The children born from the intermarriages between the godly and ungodly lines followed their example, growing up to be famous warriors and proud rulers. They built their fame on violence and oppression rather than walking with God.

differ.view: Some believe the Nephilim were an unnatural race of giants fathered specifically by fallen angels.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern writers claim the Nephilim were space aliens or rock creatures, but the text describes actual human beings.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars compare this passage to ancient Jewish traditions where rebel angels called Watchers crossed the boundary into the human realm and produced monstrous offspring.

notes.meaning: God saw how deeply evil had spread across all of human life on the earth. The problem reached all the way to the heart, where every thought, motive, and inner plan was constantly and completely wicked. There was no good left in their imaginations, showing how thoroughly sin had ruined human nature.

The Bible uses human words to describe God's holy sorrow and hatred of sin. God does not literally change his mind or lose his eternal peace, but his outward actions changed from showing favor to bringing judgment. Sin deeply wounds God's loving purposes, just like a wayward child grieves a loving father.

God decided to wipe corrupt humanity completely off the earth, just like wiping away dirt. Because the animal kingdom was made to serve human beings, the beasts, birds, and creeping things would be swept away in the same destruction. God's severe judgment shows how deeply human sin pollutes the entire creation around it.

While the rest of the world sank into total corruption, Noah received God's unearned mercy and goodwill. Finding grace means God looked upon him with kindness and chose to rescue him from the coming ruin. Even when the majority of society turns away from God, the Lord sees and cares for those who trust him.

differ.view: Noah found grace solely through God's free choice and preventing grace, which produced Noah's faith and upright living in the first place.
Noah was corrupt by nature like all men, but he was renewed in his heart and received God's favor through repentance and personal, active faith.

notes.meaning: Noah was a righteous man who lived with honest integrity before the people of his day. Being blameless does not mean he was entirely sinless, but that he was sincere, genuine, and free from hypocrisy. Like his ancestor Enoch, he lived every day in close fellowship and constant obedience with God.

differ.view: Some hold that blameless in his generations means Noah's physical bloodline remained pure from demonic intermarriage.

notes.meaning: Noah had three sons named Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Even during a dark and grieving time in the world, God provided Noah with a family. Through these three sons, God would preserve a remnant to repopulate the earth after the coming flood.

The whole earth had become rotten in God's sight, and human society was filled with violence. People completely rejected true worship and showed no fear of God. With no moral restraint, injustice, robbery, and murder ran wild everywhere.

God looked down and saw firsthand that the world had turned completely away from the right path. This corruption was not limited to one city or nation, but had infected all of mankind. The universal spread of this moral sickness showed that judgment could no longer be held back.

God shared his secret plan with Noah, announcing that human evil had reached its absolute limit. Because people had ruined the earth through their cruelty and violence, God decreed that he would destroy them along with the earth. When human sin reaches full measure, God's righteous judgment is sure to follow.

God commanded Noah to build an ark, which was a large floating chest made of durable cypress wood. It was to be divided into small rooms or compartments to hold the various animals and their supplies. Noah was told to coat it with waterproof tar both inside and outside to keep out water and block foul odors.

God gave Noah specific dimensions so the vessel would be perfectly balanced and large enough to carry out its mission. Measuring by cubits (the length from an elbow to the tip of the middle finger), the ark was about 450 to 500 feet long, 75 to 90 feet wide, and 45 to 50 feet high. Its enormous volume was designed not for sailing, but purely for floating safely on top of the water.

Noah was told to make an opening near the roof to let in fresh air and light, and to put a single door on the side of the ark. He was also commanded to divide the interior into lower, second, and third decks. This three-story structure provided plenty of organized space for living quarters, animal pens, and food storage.

God warned that he himself would unleash a great flood of waters upon the earth. The waters would destroy every living creature under the sky that breathed air. This judgment was completely certain because God’s own almighty justice was bringing it about.

God promised to establish his covenant—a solemn, binding promise—with Noah alone. Under this promise, Noah, his wife, his three sons, and his sons' wives would safely enter the ark and be preserved. Even when judgment swept away the rest of the world, God stayed faithful to his chosen servant and his household.

Noah was commanded to take two of every kind of land animal into the ark, both a male and a female. God chose to preserve the creatures he had already created rather than making an entirely new world from scratch. By bringing pairs of each kind, the animal kingdom would survive the waters and be able to reproduce later.

Pairs of every kind of bird, large animal, and creeping creature would come straight to Noah so they could be kept alive. Noah did not need to hunt or capture wild beasts by his own strength. God himself would lead the animals to the ark, showing his sovereign control over his creation.

Noah was instructed to gather and store every sort of food that people and animals needed to eat. Gathering and drying provisions for a whole year required huge effort, organization, and patience. God provided the way of rescue, but he still called Noah to work diligently to care for his family and the animals on board.

Noah followed every single instruction God gave him without adding to it or leaving anything out. Even though the task took decades, cost enormous effort, and brought ridicule from his neighbors, Noah persevered in obedience. His faithful work proved that he truly trusted God's warning about what was coming.
